title: The power path
alt: A face-on section from the street to the data hall on a normal day. The City's cable runs under the street to a vault under the sidewalk, beside a streetlight. A cable under the yard runs past the property-line fence to a pad-mounted transformer. Another cable enters the electrical room, where the switchgear, the UPS and three battery cabinets stand; a red 1 h fire-rated wall separates the electrical room from the data hall. A busway along the data-hall ceiling drops power into every server rack. Power is drawn as a dark navy cable with a travelling pulse.
sources: Grid feed 25 kV (Vancouver primary service): BC Hydro Terms and Conditions 3.7 and 3.13, effective 1 April 2026
480 V after the transformer: Schneider Galaxy VX 1000 kW UPS input, maker data
About 7 to 8 kW per rack on average: Uptime Institute Global Data Center Survey 2024, p. 10 (industry survey)
10 to 15 minutes of battery ride-through as specified: FM Global Data Sheet 5-32, 3.5.2.1 (insurer guidance; figure and clause only)
Electrical room separated by a 1 h fire separation: National Building Code of Canada 2020 and Vancouver Building By-law, Div. B 3.6.2.1.(6) and (7) (service rooms)
drawn_generically: street, sidewalk, streetlight, vault, fence, transformer, switchgear, UPS, battery cabinets, busway and racks: generic shapes in the shared visual language, not a specific product or layout
the order of the path follows the tool's power chain

camera: pans along the section, one view per step; the last step shows the whole path

steps.caption: Power comes from the City's grid in a cable under the street. It reaches the site at a vault under the sidewalk.
A cable under the yard takes it to the pad-mounted transformer, which lowers the voltage for the building.
Inside, the switchgear takes the power in and protects every circuit. A 1 h fire-rated wall separates this electrical room from the data hall.
The UPS keeps the power steady and clean. Its batteries stand by in case the grid fails.
A busway along the ceiling drops power into every server rack.
The whole path, from the street to the servers.
